Handcrafted from locally sourced hardwood with softly rounded ends, it spans the tub with guard rails underneath that hold it steady against the rim, so it won't slide or tip into the water. title: The Cornerstone Block
intro: The Cornerstone Block is the piece the rest of your kitchen answers to. Built end grain from locally sourced black walnut, each block is cut, turned, and glued up by hand into a pattern that shifts with the light, then finished with a slim brass inlay set into its edge like a maker's signature. End grain is kinder to your knives, too: the blade slips between the fibers instead of across them, so edges stay sharp and cut marks close back up. Raised feet keep it steady on the counter, and its softened edges make it as much a centerpiece as a workhorse. Add a name, date, or monogram to make it an heirloom from day one.

title: Yakisugi Crane Stool
intro: The Yakisugi Crane Stool began as a study in contrast — old technique, quiet drama. Its solid-wood frame is finished using the centuries-old Japanese yakisugi method, in which the surface is deliberately charred to deepen the grain and harden the wood against wear. Across that darkened surface, a crane is painted by hand: the traditional symbol of longevity and quiet strength. The result works as a seat, a footrest, or a low pedestal — and reads, unmistakably, as art. Only one is made; no reproductions will follow. Set it in an entryway, beside a reading chair, or anywhere a room could use a moment of stillness.
